notes: Overall a solid implementation with clean structure, but several issues drag scores down. Architectural: Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is violated in router.ts — the comment POST handler directly calls userService.getUser() and taskService.getTask() to validate and extract names before calling commentService.createComment(). This cross-service orchestration in the router is borderline acceptable (router is allowed to call services), but passing taskTitle and authorName into commentService couples the router to data it shouldn't need to fetch — the comment service ideally should not require denormalized data from other services' stores. Rule 2 is largely respected. Rule 3 is followed. Rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly implemented. Completeness: The comment.added notification logic is broken — it notifies the *author* of their own comment ('Your comment was added') rather than notifying the task assignee or other relevant parties; there is no mechanism to look up the assignee from within NotificationService (which would require cross-service data access or richer event payloads), so the notification for comment.added is functionally wrong. The DELETE /projects/:id/members route reads body from a DELETE request, but parseRequest() skips body parsing for DELETE methods, meaning removeMember will receive undefined userId and silently fail. No input validation (missing required fields, invalid email format, duplicate emails). No 'listAll tasks' endpoint without projectId filter. Code Quality: Clean, idiomatic TypeScript, good use of Map, consistent patterns, good type exports. Minor issues: require('http') inside demo.ts instead of import at top, async log() function is unnecessarily async, no error discrimination (changeStatus returns null for both 'not found' and 'invalid transition' making it impossible for the router to return a proper 400 vs 404). ConstraintCompliance: No external npm dependencies — compliant. Each service in its own file — compliant. Event bus used for inter-service communication — mostly compliant but the router orchestrates cross-service data fetching as a workaround. The DELETE body parsing bug is a functional constraint violation. The comment notification targets the wrong user, undermining the notification system's purpose.
